subject: Capacity top-up + rate-card ask — change order draft and SOW clarification
messages:
From: Anna Lopez <anna@fuseai.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-09T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Capacity top-up and rate request for Q3 order form

Hi Karthik,

We’re planning to increase forecasted usage for Q3 and want to add 200k token units to our existing order form. Given the volume, our procurement team is asking if we can revisit the rate card for per-token pricing (proposal: a 12% discount on the committed tier) and confirm proration for the remainder of the quarter.

Also need a short SOW edit that clarifies peak burst behavior (up to 4x baseline burst) and a latency SLO for 99th percentile at 250ms for gateway endpoints.

Can you send a change order draft and provide an expected timeline for signatures? We’re aiming to have this in place by June 1.

Thanks,
Anna
Anna Lopez
Head of Cloud Ops, FuseAI
anna@fuseai.com

Attachment: fuseai_capacity_request.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Subject: Re: Capacity top-up and rate request for Q3 order form

Thanks Anna — appreciate the heads up and the spreadsheet.

Short plan: I attached a first-pass change order that (a) adds the 200k committed tokens, (b) includes a line for the temporary burst allowance you mentioned, and (c) proposes the requested 12% uplift on committed-tier pricing as a commercial concession for the Q3 term. Laura, can you take a look at the redlines I flagged (billing/proration + SOW language around burst and SLO)? Stephanie, looping you since you own implementation timing and can confirm the feasibility of the 250ms p99 target for FuseAI’s gateway configuration.

Next steps I propose:
- Laura to provide legal redlines by EOD 10-May.
- I’ll send updated draft to Fuse procurement once legal and ENG sign off.
- Target DocuSign send 20-May to meet June 1 effective date.

Date: 2027-05-10T09:16:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity top-up and rate request for Q3 order form — legal redlines

Karthik — reviewed the draft. High level notes (see attached redline):
1) Billing/proration: Prefer explicit language that proration is applied pro rata based on effective date through the end of the current billing term; cap the minimum proration to one full billing unit to avoid micro-billing.
2) Burst behavior and SOW: We should limit the burst allowance to a defined "burst window" (e.g., 30 minutes sustained) and state that persistent increases beyond burst require revisiting committed quantities.
3) SLO language: Avoid hard financial penalties on p99 latency in the change order. Propose operational SLO with remediation path (technical runbook + credits ladder) instead of immediate fee deductions.
4) Term/renewal: If they want a discounted rate, add a clause that discounts are contingent on a 90-day notice for reductions and a minimum 6-month committed term for the upgraded tier.

I attached the redlined document with inline comments. If FuseAI insists on hard penalty language for latency, we'll need sign-off from legal ops and revenue for precedent.

Attachment: proposed_change_order_draft_v1_redlines.docx

- Laura
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

From: Anna Lopez <anna@fuseai.com>

Cc: procurement@fuseai.com
Date: 2027-05-10T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity top-up and rate request for Q3 order form

Thanks Karthik and Laura — quick clarifications from our side after reviewing your notes: 

- Proration: Fuse would prefer the proration be to the nearest full month (not day-level) to keep billing predictable for finance. Is that acceptable?
- Burst window: The 30-minute sustained window sounds fine. We’d like the SOW to also explicitly call out how burst is measured (concurrent tokens/sec vs. sustained tokens/min) — our engineers prefer tokens/min for telemetry granularity.
- Latency SLO: We can accept an operational SLO and the remediation ladder, but procurement wants a defined credit cap if the SLO is missed (not a per-incident automatic fee). Can you propose a capped credit schedule?

Also, one more ask: For dedicated deployment customers (we’re on Dedicated), does the latency SLO apply only to the gateway endpoints or to the inference node end-to-end? We want the SLO to cover end-to-end.

If you can incorporate these clarifications I can push the draft to legal/procurement on our side quickly.

Thanks,
Anna

Attachment: fuseai_pricing_terms_questions.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Lopez <anna@fuseai.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-11T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity top-up and rate request for Q3 order form — agreed next steps

Anna — thanks for the fast turnaround and the clarifications. Agreed approach and next steps: 

- Proration: We’ll revise proration language to "nearest full month" for predictable invoicing.
- Burst measurement: We'll use tokens/min as the measurement unit and add a short definition to the SOW. Burst window will be 30 minutes sustained as Laura recommended.
- Latency SLO & credits: We’ll propose an operational SLO with a capped quarterly credit schedule (example: up to 2% of quarterly invoice for repeated breaches, with the first missed period remediated via support runbook and a notice window). Exact caps to be finalized by RevOps/legal but we’ll provide a draft schedule in the next revision.

Action items owned: 
- Laura: incorporate proration + SOW/burst wording and draft credit cap language into redline (owner: Laura) — target EOD 12-May.
- Stephanie: confirm 250ms p99 feasibility for Dedicated and whether end-to-end measurement is supported by current telemetry (owner: Stephanie) — target 12-May.
- Karthik: consolidate final draft and send to Fuse procurement with DocuSign link for signature targeting 20-May (owner: Karthik).

I’ve attached the updated change order that includes Laura’s high-level redlines and placeholders for the credit ladder. Once we have Laura/Stephanie sign-off I’ll send the DocuSign invite and include the effective date language to hit June 1 if signed by 20-May.
